Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

wedding noun

also weddings, marriage (the ceremony), wedding day, wedding feast, nuptials, get ready for the wedding

classical

Ter. And. 47: nōn sunt vērae nūptiae
Ter. Ph. 701: apparandīs nūptiīs
Traupman 405

1nūptiae: long u (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). From nūbō, nūpsī, nūptum, which Lewis & Short marks long; the participle and its derivatives keep the vowel of the verb (nūpta).

nūptiae1, nūptiārum f. pl.

noun, first declension, plural only

a wedding, the marriage ceremony and feast

Always plural. nūptiās facere, hold a wedding (Plaut. Aul. 2.4.9, Lewis & Short); nūptiās apparāre, get it ready (Ter. Ph. 701). The wedding day is diēs nūptiārum and anything belonging to it nūptiālis, as nūptiāle dōnum, a wedding present (Traupman 405).

Examples

  • Quās crēdis esse hās nōn sunt vērae nūptiae.

    This wedding you think is going on is not a real one.Ter. And. 47

  • Spatium quidem tandem apparandīs nūptiīs, vocandī, sacrificandī dabitur paululum.

    Surely a little time will be given for getting the wedding ready, sending the invitations and offering the sacrifice.Ter. Ph. 701–702

See also marriage, marry, propose, party, celebrate, invite.

SourcesLewis & Short: nuptiae · Lewis & Short: nuptialis

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 405.
